body:
The purpose of PR #2118 was to make ` CollectionAssert.AreEqual` operate exactly as you describe. The intention was that you would not use `CollectionAssert` if you didn't want that behavior, but instead `Assert.AreEqual`.

I'm closing this as not a bug, but you can still comment and we will respond.

Well, the point of #2097 was that NUnit should __not__ be using an IEquatable implementation when we were asked to compare two collections. At first, we resisted, but the logic is that **Collection**Assert demands collection logic even if the collection object has an IEquatable implementation.

As I think about it, you may have a point. The same logic that got us to agree to the change would seem to say that it's only the __top-level__ collection that this should apply to, not the members. 

What do @nunit/framework-team members think about this? Should I reopen?
I agree to reopen. I missed this outcome earlier.

Two ways to go...
1. Apply to top level collection only
2. Apply to any members, but only if they are collections (i.e. IEnumerable)
I think (1) should be the default.
Going to pick this one up 😄

@OmicronPersei all yours, enjoy 😄 

I have assigned you to the issue, but you should be able to assign yourself now as you take issues.
Noted!  Just wanted to make sure someone else didn't want to take it up for some reason..

Wrapping my head around this one...

So what we're saying is that `CollectionAssert.AreEqual` should ignore any `IEquatable` implementation of the top level collection, but **use** any `IEquatable` implementation on the members of the collection itself to determine equality, even if the members of the top level collection are collections themselves?
